title: Proxmox VE lab: a three-node cluster and a container that survives its node
summary: Three Proxmox VE 9.2 nodes (ZFS mirror each) clustered over an isolated segment (10.10.10.0/24), and a Debian Xfce client with a browser on the same segment. Node 1 runs two LXC containers, IT-Tools and Glance. The exercises read the cluster, replicate a container's ZFS disk to the other nodes, put it under high availability, move it by hand, and finally power its node off: HA fences the dead node and starts the container on another one, with the same address, while the client keeps asking for the page.

exercises.title: The cluster
exercises.text: Corosync keeps the three nodes in one cluster over the lab segment, and /etc/pve is the same file system on every node (pmxcfs). A cluster acts only while a majority of its nodes, the quorum, see each other: two of three is enough. The web GUI of any node manages all of them: https://127.0.0.1:8006 (node 1), 8007 (node 2), 8008 (node 3), root / lab.

commands: pvecm status | sed -n '/^Name/p;/^Nodes/p;/^Quorate/p'    # pve-lab, 3 nodes, Quorate: Yes
pvecm nodes
grep ring0_addr /etc/pve/corosync.conf    # corosync on 10.10.10.2-4, the lab segment
ls /etc/pve/nodes                       # one directory per node, the same on every node

exercises.title: The containers
exercises.text: An LXC container shares the node's kernel: it starts in a second and needs a few hundred MB. CT 200 (IT-Tools) and CT 201 (Glance) run on node 1, their disks are ZFS datasets on local-zfs, and each has a second interface on the lab segment, where the client reaches it.

commands: pct list
pct config 200 | grep -E '^(hostname|memory|net1|rootfs)'
zfs list -o name,used,refer | grep subvol    # each container's root file system is a dataset
pct exec 200 -- ip -4 -o addr show eth1    # 10.10.10.20
curl -s http://10.10.10.20/ | grep -o '<title>.*</title>'    # IT-Tools
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://10.10.10.21:8080/    # Glance: 200
zfs list -o name | grep subvol    # nothing: node 2 has no copy of either container

exercises.title: ZFS replication
exercises.text: Each node has its own disks: a container on local ZFS exists on one node only. A replication job sends its dataset to another node with zfs send, the first time whole and then every minute only the changes since the last snapshot. A copy that is at most a minute old is what lets another node start the container when this one is gone.

commands: pvesr create-local-job 200-0 proxmox-ve-node2 --schedule '*/1'
pvesr create-local-job 200-1 proxmox-ve-node3 --schedule '*/1'
pvesr schedule-now 200-0; pvesr schedule-now 200-1; sleep 15
pvesr status    # LastSync, a few seconds of Duration, State OK
zfs list -t all -o name,used | grep 200    # the dataset and its __replicate_ snapshot: a copy, not a running container
pct list    # empty: the container still runs on node 1

exercises.title: High availability: a planned move
exercises.text: ha-manager watches the resources it is given. The cluster elects one CRM master; each node's LRM starts and stops what it is told and arms a watchdog. A migration of a container is a restart migration: it stops on node 1, the last changes are replicated, and it starts on node 2 with the same configuration and address.

commands: ha-manager add ct:200 --state started --max_relocate 1 --max_restart 1
sleep 20; ha-manager status    # master, three lrm lines, service ct:200 (proxmox-ve, started)
ha-manager migrate ct:200 proxmox-ve-node2
sleep 40; ha-manager status | grep ct:200    # (proxmox-ve-node2, started)
curl -s http://10.10.10.20/ | grep -o '<title>.*</title>'    # the same page, now served by node 2
pvesr status    # the job toward node 2 now points at node 1: replication follows the container
ha-manager migrate ct:200 proxmox-ve
sleep 40; ha-manager status | grep ct:200    # home again

exercises.title: A node dies, the container moves
exercises.text: Pull the plug on node 1. The other two keep the quorum; after about a minute the HA master marks the service to be fenced, and when the dead node's lock expires (two minutes: by then its watchdog would have reset it, if it were only cut off) the container starts on a surviving node from the last replica. Whatever changed after the last sync is lost: that is the price of local storage. Glance, which is not under HA, simply stays down until node 1 returns.

commands: while true; do printf '%s ' $(date +%T); curl -s -m 2 http://10.10.10.20/ | grep -o '<title>IT Tools' || echo 'no answer'; sleep 5; done    # leave it running
vmctl stop proxmox-ve --force    # a power cut, not a shutdown
watch -n 3 'ha-manager status'    # started, then fence, then (proxmox-ve-node2 or node3, started): about two and a half minutes
pvecm status | sed -n '/^Nodes/p;/^Quorate/p'    # 2 nodes, Quorate: Yes
vmctl group up proxmox-lab    # node 1 comes back and rejoins: the container stays where it is
pvesr status    # the jobs now replicate from the container's new node; the one toward node 1 failed while it was off
pvesr schedule-now 200-0; sleep 15; pvesr status    # a failed job waits before retrying: run it now, before moving the container back
ha-manager migrate ct:200 proxmox-ve    # bring it home when you like
ha-manager crm-command node-maintenance enable proxmox-ve    # a planned maintenance: HA moves the resources away first
ha-manager crm-command node-maintenance disable proxmox-ve
ha-manager remove ct:200; for j in 200-0 200-1; do pvesr delete $j; done    # back to the lab as installed
